---
title: "ssoosshd identity echo"
description: "Mint a one-time link that shows your identity provider's claims, for first setup."
---

<!-- Generated by genclidocs from the cobra command tree in server/cmd. Do not edit. -->

Mints a one-time identity echo link and prints it. Whoever opens it signs in at the identity provider and sees the claims it sends: each authentication.fields entry and what it resolves to, whether the sign-in would succeed, candidates for the subject, username and groups claims and for admin.require_group, and YAML to copy or download. No admin role is needed and no mapping has to work yet; nothing is stored, and no session is created.

Run it on the server host as the service account, with the server running: the link opens the server's own page. The code rides in the link's fragment, so no access log or proxy sees it; the database holds only its SHA-256. It works once, until --ttl runs out, and minting another replaces it.

The command then waits and prints what happened: when and from which address the link was used and how the sign-in ended (an error from the code exchange or the token check, when there was one), or that it expired. It never prints claims. Ctrl-C retires an unused link. Exits non-zero unless the claims were shown.

Records auth.echo_code_minted, auth.echo_code_used and auth.echo_code_expired, whose actor for the first is local-cli. The database is never migrated: its schema must match this ssoosshd.

## Synopsis

```
ssoosshd identity echo [flags] [args]
```

## Options

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--ttl` | duration | `15m0s` | how long the link works |
